verified.catalyst: A consortium of CPP Investments and CEO Sumant Sinha is taking ReNew private for $7.02 per share in cash through a UK scheme of arrangement. Holders of about 51.1% of the voting power have signed irrevocable undertakings, and close is guided to Q1 2027.
verified.dated_milestone: Scheme agreement 2026-08-11 (final $7.02 proposal dated 2026-07-27, confirmatory letter 2026-08-06). Next steps are the court meeting and general meeting, then the sanction hearing. The scheme-meeting dates were not found in any public source (gap). Expected close is Q1 2027.
verified.instrument: RNW common (NASDAQ). Cash-election arb; anyone not electing the rollover by the court hearing gets the cash by default.
verified.bloom_gates: G1 passes: named counterparties (CPP Investments as Purchaser, plus Sumant Sinha). G2 passes: signed scheme with 51.1% irrevocables. G3 is weak: the only unpriced figure left is a 2.3% gross spread.
verified.edge: L. The deal is real, contractual and forward, but almost all of it is already in the price. Run-up from the pre-proposal base (about $5.8-6.0, using the 200-day average of $5.97; 52-week low $4.385) to $6.865 today is roughly +15-17%. Remaining from $6.865 to the $7.02 cash price is +2.26% gross, about 5-6% annualized over a Q1 2027 close. That is near cash yield. Against it, the break downside is about -15-20% back to the base, and an earlier 2025 consortium bid for RNW did not complete.
verified.primary_source: FMP quote, 2026-11-02 ($6.865, 200-day average $5.97). InsideArbitrage, Aug 2026: CPP and Sinha consortium at $7.02, Q1 2027 close, 51.1% irrevocables. ReNew investor-relations 6-K files: the $7.02 BAFO and the 2026-08-06 confirmatory letter. SEC 6-K FY2026 d104914dex992.htm: scheme General Meeting definitions.
verified.analysis: The cash price is contractual, so the numerator provenance check does not apply, and 51.1% irrevocables make approval at the scheme vote very likely. Remaining capture is about 2.3% gross against about -15-20% downside if the deal breaks. On top of that, the 2025 bid failed and Indian regulatory and court timing is uncertain, so the trade is mostly harvested and the asymmetry is poor. Score is capped at 4 under the residual-capture rule. Keep it on WATCH for a spread widening (for example above 6%) or for the court-meeting date to be confirmed. Gap: I could not verify the court and general meeting dates or the Oct-28 side letter.

verified.catalyst: Rayonier Advanced Materials is running a formal strategic review (sale of all or part, strategic investment, merger, or the standalone plan) with Morgan Stanley and Wachtell. Management has guided that it will conclude the review and announce a path in Q4-2026.
verified.dated_milestone: Q3-2026 earnings around 2026-11-04 (estimated; first chance for a review update). Review outcome guided for Q4-2026, so by 2026-12-31. The April release said the board set no firm timetable.
verified.bloom_gates: G2 partial: the Q4-2026 conclusion is a concrete, dated management commitment, but only to announce a path, not to sell. G1 not met: AIP is a named bidder, but its offer was made around Nov-2025, rejected in Dec-2025 and disclosed in Feb-2026, with no evidence it is still live. G3 not met: there is no contractual price; the $11-12 is a stale, rejected indication.
verified.edge: M-L. Run-up: none. The stock is $6.77, about 22% below its 200-day average of $8.67, 43% below the $11.85 52-week high, and +26% off the $5.38 low. Whatever bid premium was priced in after the AIP disclosure has largely bled out. Remaining: +62-77% to the old $11-12 AIP level only if a sale happens at that price. The downside if the review ends standalone is roughly the low end ($5.4-5.5, -20%). A rough binary (about 40% sale at about $10, 60% standalone at about $5.5) gives an expected value near $7.3, about +8%. The capital structure has no preferred ahead of the common but about $779M of debt against a $458M market cap with interest coverage near 0.1x, so any sale value flows to the equity only after a heavy debt load. That leverage makes a rejected 2025 per-share bid an unreliable anchor today.
verified.primary_source: RYAM Q2-2026 earnings release, 8-K dated 2026-08-04 (sec.gov ex99-1), and the 10-Q for the period ended 2026-06-27: both state the review will conclude in Q4-2026. Jax Daily Record 2026-04-20 on the review launch and the AIP bid history. FMP quote 2026-11-02: $6.77, market cap $458M, 200-day average $8.67, 52-week range $5.38-11.85.
verified.analysis: The dated window is real: the Q2 release (2026-08-04) and the 10-Q both say the review concludes in Q4-2026. But there is no named live counterparty and no price, and the falling price says the market thinks a sale at the old AIP level is unlikely. The option value is cheap because the bid premium has largely been given back, but the event is a coin flip with a credible standalone downside on a heavily levered balance sheet. It stays WATCH, to be revisited at Q3 earnings (about 11-04). Gap: I found no Q3 release, 8-K or October news on the review. Debt is from an undated Simply Wall St snapshot, not re-derived from the latest 10-Q.

verified.catalyst: Topline data are due in mid-December 2026 from upLIFT, the single-arm pivotal Phase 3 of ersodetug in tumor hyperinsulinism (n=16). The primary endpoint is the share of patients reaching at least a 50% cut in IV glucose infusion, and it passes if the lower bound of the 95% CI is at least 30%, meaning roughly 9 of 16 responders.
verified.dated_milestone: upLIFT topline guided for mid-Dec 2026 (enrollment completed, PR 2026-10-14). Next after that is an NDA/BLA filing decision with Breakthrough Therapy designation (granted May 2025), timing not yet guided.
verified.instrument: RZLT common (NASDAQ), $3.795 on 2026-11-02, market cap about $367M
verified.bloom_gates: G2: a concrete company commitment to mid-Dec 2026 topline with a predefined statistical bar. G3 is only partial: the readout itself is unpriced, but the interim (7 of the first 8 responders) is already public and was traded in June 2026. G1 is not applicable (no counterparty).
verified.edge: M. This is a binary with a favorable starting point. 7 of the first 8 patients met the responder bar (one cancer death counts as a non-responder), so the trial needs only about 2 more responders among the last 8. Run-up from the pre-catalyst base: +15% from the $3.30 close before the interim (2026-05-29), and about +115-200% from the post-sunRIZE crash range of $1.23-1.77 (Dec 2025). Remaining capture: about +45-70% to a success value of roughly $5.5-6.5 (the June-August post-interim range of $4.9-5.3 plus some readout de-risking), against about -65-70% to roughly $1.1-1.3 (cash backing, about $108M at 6/30/26 less burn) on failure. The probability-weighted value is about $5.0 at roughly 80% success odds, so about +30% expected. The stock has already given back from $4.87 to $3.58-3.95 on the October update, so this is not re-rated, but it is not deep value either.
verified.primary_source: Rezolute PR 'Completion of Enrollment in Phase 3 upLIFT Study' (GlobeNewswire, 2026-10-14); June 2026 positive interim PR (BioSpace); FY2026 10-K/8-K (SEC, cash $107.8M at 2026-06-30); FMP quote and EOD history (2026-11-02); Clinical Trials Arena on sunRIZE failure (2025-12-11).
verified.analysis: The catalyst is confirmed as real, dated and forward. Rezolute's 2026-10-14 PR says upLIFT is fully enrolled with topline mid-Dec 2026, and 7 of the first 8 patients met the responder criterion, so the 56% responder-rate threshold looks very achievable. The upside is limited by the small market (tumor HI is ultra-rare and ersodetug is now the company's only viable indication after the Dec-2025 sunRIZE congenital-HI failure, which cut the stock 88%). Other limits: a one-death/non-responder pattern in a cancer population, an open-label single-arm design, and likely dilution after the data, since cash was $107.8M at 6/30/26 against about $78M a year of burn. Gaps: I did not pull the latest 10-Q for exact share count or cash at 9/30, I did not verify the remaining-8 responder count beyond the October PR, and the success-case value is a heuristic from the post-interim trading range, not a rNPV.

verified.bloom_gates: G1 (named counterparty: Texas Instruments) and G2 (definitive merger agreement at $231 cash, stockholders approved). G3 not met: the remaining figure is the $8.52 spread, which is already almost fully priced.
verified.edge: L. Run-up from the pre-catalyst base: $136.62 close on 2026-02-03 to $222.48 = +62.8%. Remaining to the contractual $231 = +3.83% gross, about 6% annualized to a mid-2027 close. Break downside: the undisturbed price was around $137-145, so a break costs about 35-38%. The spread implies roughly a 10-11% break probability. This is a pure bet on how China's SAMR handles a US-semi deal during trade friction, and the market is already pricing that risk sensibly. The payoff is asymmetric to the downside, and about 90%+ of the event value is already in the price.
verified.primary_source: Silicon Labs 10-Q for the period ending 2026-07-04 (stockholder approval 2026-04-30, $231 cash, close 1H27); TXN Q1-2026 10-Q; CCS Singapore clearance release 2026-08-07; MLex 2026-06-11 (SAMR not yet accepted the filing); FMP quote 2026-11-02 at $222.48 and FMP EOD closes for 2026-02-03 ($136.62) and 2026-02-04 ($203.41).

I could not verify SAMR acceptance after the 2026-06-11 MLex report that it had not been accepted, so this is an evidence gap. At $222.48 the stock has captured about 63% from the $136.62 unaffected close, and only 3.8% gross remains against about 36% break downside. That makes it a mostly-harvested event, capped at score 4. The numerator-provenance rule does not apply because the cash price is contractual. Keep on WATCH: the actionable trigger is SAMR formally accepting the filing, or the spread widening on trade-tension headlines.
